design_references.title: Fleet CPG Engine — Phase 0 (Baseline)
design_references.claim: Joern's cold-build cost and per-invocation overhead, measured across repos of different scale and language, set the baseline the Fleet CPG Engine's O(diff)-per-PR and always-resident serving design must beat. This is the third of the four repos in that spec, the medium-scale TypeScript/React case (~173k LOC in packages/excalidraw).

hypothesis: Full joern process wall time (JVM start, CPG open, golden-query execution, teardown) is lower when Joern reuses an existing workspace project with a warm OS page cache (variant warm) than when it opens the CPG for the first time with no existing workspace project (variant cold), for excalidraw's core package (packages/excalidraw) at a pinned revision. (fleet-cpg-baseline-zod already rejected this hypothesis once at smaller scale; this run checks whether a ~2x larger CPG changes the outcome.)
null_hypothesis: Warm-variant process wall time is not meaningfully lower than cold-variant process wall time; any difference is within repetition noise.
independent_variable: Workspace/page-cache state before the joern process starts (cold: no prior workspace project for this CPG; warm: workspace project and OS page cache already populated by the immediately preceding cold run). The CPG binary, source revision, and query set are held fixed.

environment.network_justification: Materializes the pinned excalidraw revision via `git clone` from github.com. Joern is already installed locally from the fleet-cpg-baseline-zod run; no repeat download.

variants.name: cold
variants.description: Fresh workspace: no prior joern project for this CPG, unwarmed OS page cache for the CPG's on-disk representation.

variants.name: warm
variants.description: Reused workspace: joern project from the immediately preceding cold run still present, OS page cache warm.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Accept: median warm process_wall_time_ms is at least 20% lower than median cold process_wall_time_ms, across all 3 repetitions. Reject: the two medians are within 20% of each other, or warm is higher. Either way, cold_build wall time and peak RSS from cold_build.log are reported as the Phase 0 baseline deliverable, independent of this hypothesis's outcome.

evaluator.rubric: Score each query row on: (1) status == "ok" for every query in the golden set — any "error:*" status is a hard failure of the benchmark, not a data point to average away; (2) result_count is stable across all repetitions of the same (query_id, variant) pair for a fixed source revision — a changing count indicates the CPG itself is nondeterministic and invalidates the run; (3) compare median process_wall_time_ms for variant=warm against variant=cold across repetitions per the acceptance rule in metrics.acceptance_rule; (4) report cold_build wall time and peak RSS from cold_build.log as baseline numbers regardless of the cold/warm outcome — they are the Phase 0 deliverable even if the cache-state hypothesis is rejected.
